data.title: How much will it cost to prevent another air traffic meltdown?
data.description:
• Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy used his appearance at a Friday night White House News conference to call for billions in emergency funding to prevent another nationwide ground stop.
  • "I've asked, the president's asked for $30 billion," he said. "I want $50 billion...What's more important than having an air traffic system that actually works?"
  • When Duffy previously called for the $30 billion funding, he said support was "bipartisan."
  • The secretary intends to hold another briefing Saturday at 1030a ET.
  • While the ground stop was lifted around 8p ET Friday, airlines are still scrambling to get stranded passengers on their way. 
  • The disruption caused more than 9,100 flight cancellations and 24,000 delays, according to data from FlightAware. 
  • On Saturday morning, more than 3,500 additional flights were cancelled with another 1,400 delays.

data.title: Adobe's new agentic tools appear impressive, but BTIG seeks more evidence of growth
data.description:
Adobe (ADBE) revealed new agentic AI tools and previewed local MCP integrations that allow creators to utilize third-party agents in Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and After Effects during its MAX event last week.

BTIG analysts said they were encouraged by the innovations but need more evidence of Adobe's growth durability before recommending a Buy on the stock. As a result, the financial services firm maintained its Neutral rating.

"In this new era, mgmt. noted customers want to see value of a product prior to making any purchasing decisions, and the company is orienting GTM and product efforts around showing customers immediate value, especially as new pricing methodologies emerge (e.g., consumption, outcome, etc.)," said BTIG analysts Nick Altmann and Nick Dannewitz in an investor report. "As part of their effort to engage with customers and ease the adoption curve, ADBE is experimenting with week-to-week contracts for its Acrobat offering. This comes after ADBE has seen a significant increase in its month-to-month contracts."

"In the future, ADBE sees a world combining headless workflows with direct customer interaction within ADBE's platform, and ADBE announced new local Creative Cloud MCP integrations, which will let third-party agents work directly within Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, and After Effects," they added.

Adobe also announced a new partnership with Disney (DIS).

"This is likely ADBE's most important Firefly Foundry partnership and deal yet, and success could usher in additional interest from other media entities," Altmann wrote.

BTIG currently forecasts that Adobe's full-year fiscal 2026 revenue will increase by 12% year over year and by 10% in fiscal year 2027. It projects free cash flow margins of 40% and 41%, respectively.

data.title: The Grand Theft Auto 6 economy reaches far and wide
data.description:
The release of Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 19 is projected to generate massive interest in the video game industry after the 13-year wait since the last installment in the series. At launch, the game will be available exclusively on PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, and Xbox Series X|S, with legacy Xbox One owners able to stream it via Xbox Cloud Gaming, while PC and Nintendo Switch 2 players are left waiting for a later release window. In North America, digital access opens at 12:00 AM ET on November 19, meaning players on the U.S. West Coast can start playing at 9:00 PM PT on Wednesday, November 18, while players in the United Kingdom and Oceania unlock at 12:00 AM local time. Pre-loads went live on November 10, requiring roughly 212 GB of storage space, and the standard edition carries a $79.99 price tag. For investors, the broad GTA 6 economy may be worth watching for an interesting trade.

Take-Two Interactive (TTWO): Wall Street and industry analysts have set historic benchmarks for the release, fueled by Take-Two (TTWO) CEO Strauss Zelnick noting pre-orders are running "far in excess" of internal expectations. Data trackers like Sensor Tower estimated roughly 10M digital pre-orders days ahead of launch, with an unusually high concentration of buyers opting for higher-priced special editions like the $99.99 tier. Analysts project roughly $600M in profit for Take-Two from the initial launch window alone, anchoring the company's full-year FY2027 net bookings guidance of $8.0B to $8.2B, a roughly 20.5% jump over the prior year. Long-term models anticipate GTA VI’s online component eventually capturing around 60M monthly active users, pushing bullish Wall Street price targets for Take-Two into the $310 to $330 range. Bank of America expects a press release from the company within the first few days of the release if the launch stats are strong.

Sony (SONY) and Microsoft (MSFT): Console makers stand to earn steady, lower-risk upside from GTA 6. Sony (SONY), with roughly 98M PS5 consoles shipped, collects a standard platform cut on digital copies and in-game purchases, and could see added engagement across PlayStation Network. Microsoft (MSFT) earns a similar cut on Xbox Series X|S sales. GTA 6 is not part of Game Pass, but Xbox One owners can stream it by buying the game and cloud playtime, which could generate cloud-hour revenue even as it reduces the need to buy a new console. Notably, gaming console trends have improved in the last few months, and the holidays provide an opportunity for the momentum to extend.

AMD (AMD): Underneath the console hoods, AMD (AMD) supplies the custom semi-custom APUs powering every single native launch console, which means a holiday hardware bundle surge could boost royalties and chip orders.

Retail: Brick-and-mortar and online retailers such as GameStop (GME), Best Buy (BBY), Walmart (MWT), Target (TGT), and Amazon (AMZN) expect to see extra sales tied to gaming equipment and consoles, as rare midnight launches and high-margin accessory attach rates on controllers and headsets factor in. Also in the mix, Turtle Beach (HEAR) and Corsair (CRSR) could benefit, as both sell gaming peripherals such as headsets and controllers. Further down the list of beneficiaries, DoorDash (DASH) and Uber Eats (UBER) expect to see a short-term wave of extra demand from gamers.

Movie theater stocks: GTA 6 is expected to dominate social media feeds and streaming platforms in a development that could make it harder for studios to create viral buzz over major tentpole film releases in late November and December. Analysts also warn of a minor box office headwind for chains such as AMC Entertainment (AMC) and Cinemark (CNK), with young male walk-up traffic expected to be softer than normal.

Digital content: Amazon's (AMZN) Twitch, Alphabet's (GOOG) (GOOGL) YouTube, and Discord (DSCD) are poised to see a surge in viewership and engagement metrics, driven by creator streams and roleplay communities forming. 

Logitech (LOGI): Big game launches tend to spark purchases of controllers, headsets, keyboards, and other accessories. The tech company is also creating buzz by giving employees an extra day off to play a video game of their choice.

Notable ETFs focused on the video game and esports sector include the VanEck Video Gaming and eSports ETF (ESPO), the Global X Video Games & Esports ETF (HERO), and the Roundhill Video Games ETF (NERD).

Merlin Properties signals 2026 FFO guidance of €0.58 as it reshapes 704 MW data center plan amid Spain’s Royal Decree
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: MERLIN Properties SOCIMI, S.A. (MPTYY) Q3 2026

Management view

  • Despite “the emotional rollercoaster during the quarter,” management said “the results of the company have remained steady and convincing,” highlighting “3.4% like-for-like growth in offices, shopping centers and logistics,” “very high occupancy overall… at 95%,” and that “the FFO has increased also by 11.9%,” according to (Executive Vice-Chairman & CEO Ismael Orrego).

  • Management raised full-year guidance, with (Executive Vice-Chairman & CEO Orrego) saying: “we are in a position to increase our expected full year 2026 guidance to EUR 0.58 versus EUR 0.55 before.”

  • On data centers, (Executive Vice-Chairman & CEO Orrego) said the Mega Plan pipeline expanded at the negotiation stage: “Beyond the 160 megawatts IT load, we are in advanced negotiation now for 206 megawatts, up 26 from last information disclosed to market,” while adding the “180-megawatt big contract in Portugal is not yet signed” and would be disclosed via regulator filing “given its sheer size.”

  • (Executive Vice-Chairman & CEO Orrego) framed Spain’s draft data center Royal Decree as a central stock overhang and presented a “worst-case scenario” response plan, including a revision of Phase 3 footprints and added battery storage requirements to meet “80% self-consumption with hourly correlation.”

  • Management disclosed capital recycling progress, with (Executive Vice-Chairman & CEO Orrego) stating: “regarding the noncore divestments, we are at EUR 75.4 million with EUR 66.8 million to be executed before year-end… So we are perfectly on track to be in the region of EUR 140 million as of year-end.”

  • Management announced a finance leadership change, with (Executive Vice-Chairman & CEO Orrego) introducing (CFO Javier Echave) as “new to the company… coming from Heathrow Airport in the U.K., and he’s going to be our CFO.”

  • (CFO Javier Echave) emphasized liquidity and refinancing, saying: “As of 30th of September… cash and cash equivalents stand at EUR 1.4 billion… loan-to-value is 24.9%… interest cover… is at 3.6x,” and later: “we announced a new successful… financing platform that fully removes our refinancing risk for the next 3 years,” including “2 term loans totaling EUR 2.25 billion… maturing in April 2032” and an “expanded revolving credit facility… to EUR 1.5 billion.”

Outlook

  • (Executive Vice-Chairman & CEO Orrego) upgraded 2026 guidance: “EUR 0.58 versus EUR 0.55 before,” while also cautioning, “I don’t know if we will be able to exceed it or not. I don’t — I really don’t think it.”

  • (Executive Vice-Chairman & CEO Orrego) outlined a contingency-driven change in the data center plan under a prolonged Royal Decree scenario: “the total Mega Plan moves from 724 megawatts to 704 megawatts,” and said the modeled incremental battery storage capex implied “a sunken cost… EUR 553 million, which is 7% of our total Mega Plan.”

  • Management described a scenario-driven shift in investment geography if Spain’s framework persists, with (Executive Vice-Chairman & CEO Orrego) stating: “if the situation doesn’t change, that means we will stop new developments in Spain and move production to Portugal.”

Financial results

  • Management reported operating momentum in traditional assets and cash flow, with (Executive Vice-Chairman & CEO Orrego) citing “3.4% like-for-like growth,” “occupancy… at 95%,” and “the FFO has increased also by 11.9%,” and adding, “our margins are maintained overall or even slightly improved.”

  • Balance sheet commentary centered on fixed-rate positioning and future funding runway, with (CFO Echave) stating “close to 100% of our debt remains fixed,” “average maturity has been extended to 5.7 years,” and that management “forecast to cover… more than 1/3 of Phase 3 investment… without the need to access debt nor equity markets until 2028.”

  • Management quantified an illustrative rate-up scenario through 2030, with (CFO Echave) saying: “we have assumed that our average cost of debt rises by 110 basis points to 3.8%,” and under that scenario “debt service would increase from EUR 134 million in 2025… to a potential EUR 317 million in 2030,” while “rents are expected to grow… from EUR 541 million to EUR 1.6 billion by 2030.”

Q&A

  • Mariano Miguel Hidalgo, Alantra: Asked whether Portugal could adopt restrictive regulation, asked about REN power auction timing, and requested more detail on 2027–2028 cost of debt; (Director Francisco Rivas) said Portugal’s draft is heading to “public consultation before year-end,” and that “hourly correlation… are not in the table right now,” while confirming “we are participating in that auction” expected “first quarter 2027”; (CFO Echave) declined to provide spread detail but said “99.8% of our debt is fixed debt” and “assume… no major changes in the short term.”

  • Thomas Rothaeusler, Deutsche Bank: Asked if Royal Decree capex can be offset by pricing and the yield-on-cost impact, how a Portugal mega-lease would reduce CoreWeave concentration, and where rents sit vs “EUR 120 per kilowatt”; (Executive Vice-Chairman & CEO Orrego) said if worst case becomes base case, “multiply our current yield on cost by 0.93”; (Director Rivas) said CoreWeave could be “approximately 19% of our total data center capacity” when the 704 MW is deployed and provided rent levels: “126 in Phase 1… 132 in Phase 2… Phase 3, 135.”

  • Florent Laroche-Joubert, ODDO BHF: Asked if appraisers could factor the worst-case scenario into year-end valuation and asked about demand resilience amid political debate; (Executive Vice-Chairman & CEO Orrego) said tenants are “completely unaffected,” described lengthening tenant compulsories (“You will offer… 10 years… they would say… 15 years”), and stated that appraisers focus on enforceability: “what they see is a compulsory contract… under Spanish or Portuguese law.”

  • Aaron Guy, Citi: Asked about demand dynamics and whether equipment procurement could delay builds, plus follow-ups on depreciation and tenant default remedies; (Director Rivas) said some components are “long leads” and “mainly on transformers… you’re getting there,” but “so far, there is no equipment that exceeds” typical “24 to 30 months” timelines; (Executive Vice-Chairman & CEO Orrego) challenged the market’s depreciation narrative, saying “accounting depreciation… equals tax depreciation,” and estimated a “loss of profitability due to depreciation… between 1.2% and 1.5%.”

  • José Ocina, CaixaBank (summarized by management): Asked about the reported 9.3 GW network plan for data centers, whether contingency becomes the firm plan, Arasur 4/5 counterparty, and legal strategy; (Executive Vice-Chairman & CEO Orrego) said the extra power would be “subject to complying with the Royal Decree,” confirmed “it was Solaria,” and stated, “we don’t reveal our legal strategy.”

  • Veronique Meertens, Kempen (summarized by management): Asked if BESS adds delays and when decisions are needed; (Executive Vice-Chairman & CEO Orrego) replied, “the time lines are not affected… just the capex.”

  • Marios Pastou, Bernstein (summarized by management): Asked whether Lisbon projects are tied to one end user and whether all 704 MW would comply under the modeled capex; management answered “Yes” to compliance and said Portugal’s “200 megawatts potential… is actually 750, but it is still awaiting the approval of the Portuguese government.”

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was probing and risk-focused, concentrating on Spain’s Royal Decree economics, valuation implications, tenant concentration/CoreWeave, procurement bottlenecks, and funding visibility.

  • Management’s prepared remarks were confident on operations and funding, but turned combative on regulation and CoreWeave skepticism, with (Executive Vice-Chairman & CEO Orrego) calling SRAP “SRAP crap,” saying the lack of grandfathering is “criminal,” and characterizing CoreWeave concerns as “a textbook shortselling attack.”

  • Versus the prior quarter, the Q3 call carried more defensive language and more time spent on regulatory downside framing and a quantified worst-case capex plan, while also presenting a stronger near-term funding package and a higher full-year FFO-per-share guide.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Guidance moved higher, with Q3 raising 2026 FFO per share to “EUR 0.58 versus EUR 0.55 before,” after Q2 guided “around EUR 0.55 per share.”

  • The Mega Plan perimeter changed from “724 megawatts” (Q2) to “704 megawatts” (Q3) due to the Royal Decree-driven reshaping and putting “Arasur 4 and 5… to the freezer for the moment,” per (Executive Vice-Chairman & CEO Orrego).

  • The balance-sheet narrative evolved from liquidity and preparing refinancing (Q2) to executed refinancing and pre-funding runway (Q3), with (CFO Echave) stating the new platform “fully removes our refinancing risk for the next 3 years.”

  • Analyst focus shifted from growth execution and funding triggers (Q2) to regulation mechanics (SRAD/SRAP, hourly correlation), valuation impacts under a worst case, and CoreWeave concentration/credit framing (Q3).

Risks and concerns

  • (Executive Vice-Chairman & CEO Orrego) identified regulatory uncertainty as the main risk driver, warning the Royal Decree could “dissuade data center investors,” and said the company modeled incremental battery storage, including “a total BESS CapEx of EUR 863 million.”

  • Execution and power-delivery risk featured in the Phase 3 reshaping, with (Executive Vice-Chairman & CEO Orrego) citing Arasur 4/5 issues after a partner “losing their electricity licenses,” and stating the company will only deploy projects where it has “100% certainty that we are going to get the electricity.”

  • Client concentration risk was addressed directly, with (Director Rivas) stating CoreWeave “as of the first half of 2026, represented 80.6% of our total gross rental income,” and outlining diversification plans and contractual protections (deposits, guarantees, and modular design).

Final takeaway

Management framed Q3 as steady traditional-asset performance plus accelerating data center monetization, while making Spain’s proposed Royal Decree the central uncertainty: MERLIN raised 2026 FFO per-share guidance to €0.58, quantified a worst-case compliance capex plan (including €863M of BESS capex and a 724 MW to 704 MW Mega Plan revision), and emphasized a strengthened funding position via a new refinancing platform, while also arguing that lease enforceability, demand tightness, and diversification over time can mitigate market concerns around tenant concentration and regulation-driven economics.
